decisions.rationale: "breast cancer" in the title is a standalone disease name used as the object of the preposition, not modifying another noun. It is treated as a single disease concept (not a family of diseases), so it is a Specific Disease. General term rules keep "cancer" in disease names like this.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 (Specific Disease); What NOT to Annotate 4 (cancer retained)

decisions.rationale: "breast and ovarian cancers" is a contiguous string referring to two separate diseases (breast cancer and ovarian cancer), so it is annotated as one Composite Mention rather than split, since splitting would lose information.
"cancer" in "cancer-causing deletion" is a disease mention used as a modifier of the noun "deletion," so it is annotated as a Modifier rather than a standalone disease.
